ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, under normal pressure, moist air with an air temperature of 30°C and a wet-bulb temperature of 28°C, after fully contacting a large amount of cold water in a spray chamber, is cooled into saturated air at 10°C. If the gas leaving the spray chamber is reheated to 30°C, the wet-bulb temperature of the air at this time is _\mathrm{^\circ C}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, moist air flows from left to right; the left inlet is labeled with dry-bulb temperature t and wet-bulb temperature t_w; the middle is a spray chamber, with sprayed water droplets drawn; the pipeline after leaving the spray chamber is labeled 10°C; then the airflow passes through a reheater, and the rightmost outlet is labeled 30°C. Then reason: The problem statement says that the air at the outlet of the spray chamber is saturated air at 10°C, so its water vapor partial pressure is equal to the saturated water vapor pressure at 10°C, that is, p_v=p_ws(10°C)≈1.228 kPa. During reheating to 30°C, there is no humidification and no dehumidification, so the water vapor partial pressure remains unchanged. For air after reheating with a dry-bulb temperature of 30°C, use the normal-pressure wet-bulb temperature relation p_v=p_ws(T_w)-γP(30-T_w). Substitute P=101.325 kPa and p_v=p_ws(10°C), numerically solve p_ws(10°C)=p_ws(T_w)-γP(30-T_w), and obtain T_w≈18.1°C.

raw_record.question_text: As shown in the figure, under normal pressure, moist air with an air temperature of 30°C and a wet-bulb temperature of 28°C, after fully contacting a large amount of cold water in a spray chamber, is cooled into saturated air at 10°C. If the gas leaving the spray chamber is reheated to 30°C, the wet-bulb temperature of the air at this time is _\mathrm{^\circ C}$.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: air flows through a spray chamber, exits at 10°C, then is reheated to 30°C. From the text, take normal pressure, final spray-chamber outlet as saturated 10°C air, and final dry-bulb temperature after reheating as 30°C. Because the reheater does not change moisture content, set the final vapor pressure equal to the saturation vapor pressure at 10°C. Use the standard psychrometric wet-bulb equation at 1 atm for a 30°C dry-bulb air stream, solve p_ws(10)=p_ws(T_w)-γP(30-T_w), and report the root T_w≈18.1°C.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图中湿空气从左向右流动，左侧入口标有干球温度 t 和湿球温度 t_w；中间是淋水室，画有喷淋水滴；离开淋水室后的管线上标有 10°C；随后气流经过一个再热器，最右端出口标有 30°C。再推理：题设说明淋水室出口空气为 10°C 饱和空气，因此其水蒸气分压等于 10°C 下的饱和水蒸气压，即 p_v=p_ws(10°C)≈1.228 kPa。再热到 30°C 的过程中不加湿、不除湿，所以水蒸气分压保持不变。对再热后干球温度为 30°C 的空气，用常压湿球温度关系 p_v=p_ws(T_w)-γP(30-T_w)。代入 P=101.325 kPa、p_v=p_ws(10°C)，数值求解 p_ws(10°C)=p_ws(T_w)-γP(30-T_w)，得到 T_w≈18.1°C。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct psychrometric-equation route: it avoids using the inlet-air state and instead uses the image/text process sequence to recognize that reheating occurs at constant humidity ratio after the air has become saturated at 10°C.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram as a left-to-right process: humid air enters a spray chamber, leaves it at a labeled 10°C state, then passes through a reheater and exits at a labeled 30°C state. The heater symbol indicates temperature rise without water addition/removal.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the written data: normal pressure, inlet air condition 30°C dry bulb and 28°C wet bulb, full contact with much cold water, outlet from spray chamber is saturated at 10°C, then reheated to 30°C. The inlet condition is not needed after the problem explicitly fixes the spray-chamber outlet as saturated 10°C.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: At 1 atm, saturated air at 10°C has vapor pressure equal to p_ws(10°C), and reheating without moisture change keeps vapor pressure/humidity ratio constant. The wet-bulb temperature T_w of the final 30°C air can be found from the psychrometer relation p_v = p_ws(T_w) - γP(30 - T_w), with γ≈0.00066(1+0.00115T_w) and P=101.325 kPa, using steam-table/Antoine saturation pressures. Set p_v=p_ws(10°C) and solve for T_w, giving about 18.1°C.
